bull.b: Sustained high gross and operating margins reflect strong product differentiation, pricing power and cost structure in ATE and system-test businesses. Durable margin levels provide cash flow to fund R&D, demos and strategic investments, insulating returns through normal demand cycles.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and strong ROE
bull.b: Very low leverage and historically high ROE give the company financial flexibility to invest, buy back stock, and withstand semiconductor-capex cyclicality. A conservative balance sheet reduces refinancing risk and supports multi-year capex and M&A optionality without stressing liquidity.

Structural AI and compute-driven spending creates multi-year secular demand for test equipment and related services. Teradyne's exposure to compute, HBM/DRAM and merchant GPUs positions it to capture share as wafer fab and data-center investments scale, supporting durable revenue expansion.

bear.b: The business is tightly coupled to semiconductor capital cycles, producing large revenue volatility across years. This cyclical exposure makes long-term planning for fixed costs, R&D pacing and capacity utilization harder and can compress earnings and cash flow during downturns.

Periods where operating cash lags reported earnings indicate earnings may not reliably convert to cash. That inconsistency raises execution risk for sustaining buybacks, dividends and R&D during weaker quarters and complicates capital-allocation timing over the medium term.

bear.t: Margin and working-capital pressure from memory and inventory
bear.b: Management cited persistent memory-related margin headwinds and elevated inventory builds to support expected sales. Inventory ties up cash and risks obsolescence; combined with memory-margin pressure this can limit margin expansion and constrain free cash flow if demand timing shifts.
